intro: Bošáca has produced three of Slovakia's national tree champions from one stretch of countryside. An heirloom apple, about 130 years old, won in 2017 and placed sixth in Europe; a rare pink-fleshed pear, roughly 200 years old, won in 2015 and placed third; and a wild pear on nearby Lysica Hill, about 150 years old, won in 2024 and placed fifth. The apple and older pear stand 350 metres apart in the hamlet of Zabudišová; the wild pear stands four kilometres off. No other Slovak village has produced three champions.
meta_description: Three Slovak Tree of the Year champions, an heirloom apple, a rare pink pear and a self-seeded wild pear, all growing in and around the village of Bošáca.
question_meta: Bošáca's oldest documented tree is the Pink Pear of Zabudišová, roughly 200 years old; an heirloom apple and a wild pear on Lysica Hill are both younger.
question_answer: Bošáca's oldest documented tree is the Pink Pear of Zabudišová, a heirloom variety estimated at roughly 200 years old and Slovakia's 2015 Tree of the Year; the heirloom apple growing 350 metres away is younger, about 130 years old and the 2017 champion, and the Wild Pear of Lysica Hill, about 150 years old and the 2024 champion, is younger still.
question_context: The apple and the older pear grow in Zabudišová, a hillside hamlet of Bošáca in western Slovakia, and all three trees here are national tree champions. The pear, Bošácka ružová, is a pink-fleshed variety that won Slovakia's Strom roka title in 2015, then placed third at the European final, its age given as around 200 years by two independent Slovak outlets; local tradition ties it to the area's first settlers, known for making fruit brandy from orchards like this one. The apple carries the rare local variety Citrónové zimné Zabudišovské, planted an estimated 130 years ago, and won the same contest in 2017, placing sixth in Europe; its girth was measured at 251 centimetres. Four kilometres away, on the slope at the foot of Lysica Hill, a wild pear grew from a stray seed; it won the 2024 title and placed fifth in Europe in 2025, its trunk 195 centimetres round. All three stand on open ground with no gate or ticket, roughly 15 minutes by car from Nové Mesto nad Váhom.

faq.q: What is the oldest tree in Bošáca?
faq.a: The Pink Pear of Zabudišová, estimated at roughly 200 years old and Slovakia's 2015 Tree of the Year. The heirloom apple 350 metres away is younger, about 130 years old, and the Wild Pear of Lysica Hill, four kilometres off, is younger still at roughly 150.

faq.q: Are all three trees free to visit?
faq.a: Yes. All three stand on open farmland or hillside with no gate, ticket or permission needed.

faq.q: How do the three trees compare?
faq.a: The pear of Zabudišová is oldest at roughly 200 years, ahead of the wild pear on Lysica Hill at about 150 and the apple at about 130. The Zabudišová pear also placed highest in Europe, third, against fifth for the Lysica Hill pear and sixth for the apple.

faq.q: Why has one village produced three national tree champions?
faq.a: Nobody claims to know for certain, though the Bošácka valley has a long fruit-growing tradition and self-seeded wild pears are said to be a feature of the White Carpathians landscape here. No other Slovak village has won the national Tree of the Year contest three times.

The apple and pear stand in the Zabudišová locality of Bošáca; the wild pear stands on Lysica Hill, four kilometres away. All are in the Nové Mesto nad Váhom district, roughly 15 minutes by car from the nearest town. There is no public transport stop at any of the trees.

trees.name: The Apple Tree of Zabudišová

location.address: roadside in the Zabudišová locality, Bošáca, Nové Mesto nad Váhom District

trees.story:
In 2017 a nearly forgotten apple variety beat every other tree in Slovakia to become that year's national Tree of the Year, then went on to place sixth in the European final the following spring.

Nobody had paid the tree much attention before the contest. It grows on a roadside in Zabudišová, a scattered hamlet of the village of Bošáca, and belongs to Citrónové zimné Zabudišovské, a lemon-yellow winter apple bred locally and grown almost nowhere else. Itinerant fruit-growers, tradesmen who planted orchards for a living and moved on, are thought to have put it in the ground roughly 130 years ago. When it won, it measured two and a half metres round and stood thirteen metres tall, dimensions that make sense for an apple tree left alone for well over a century.

It still fruits. The variety's practical value, a fruit that keeps through winter without a cellar, is presumably why somebody planted it here in the first place, long before there was a competition to win.

Three hundred and fifty metres away, on the same hillside, stands another Slovak Tree of the Year: a pink-fleshed pear that won two years earlier. Two national champions from one small stretch of Zabudišová, which almost nobody outside Bošáca seems to know.
trees.access: Free, roadside tree on a public lane in the Zabudišová part of the village; no gate or permission needed.
trees.transport: Rural village lane, Bošáca; nearest town Nové Mesto nad Váhom roughly 15 minutes by car.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the roadside apple tree, about 2.5m round, distinct from the pink-fleshed pear standing 350m away on the same hillside. It stands on a lane in the Zabudisova part of Bosaca.

trees.name: The Pink Pear of Zabudišová

location.address: near the Zabudišová locality, Bošáca, Nové Mesto nad Váhom District

trees.story:
Slovakia's national tree contest has been won only once by a pear, and this pink-fleshed local variety is it.

Bošácka ružová grows almost nowhere outside this stretch of the Bošáca countryside: a pear whose flesh runs pink rather than white, a curiosity local orchardists have kept going for generations. In 2015 it won the national Strom roka title, then went to the European final and placed third, an unusually strong result for a tree nobody outside its own region had heard of a year earlier.

Local tradition holds that it was planted by the area's first settlers, known for making fruit brandy from orchards like this one, though nothing pins that to a date. Two separate outlets covering its 2015 win, pravda.sk and teraz.sk, independently give its age as about two hundred years, which this page repeats with confidence. Nobody has published a reliable girth or height for this specific tree, so those stay open. What is confirmed, from the region's own tourism writing, is a solitary tree on open land near Zabudišová, unfenced and reachable without asking anyone.

It stands 350 metres from another national champion, an heirloom apple that won two years later. Two prize-winning fruit trees, in one small corner of western Slovakia, planted for eating rather than for looking at. If you have measured its girth, tell us.
trees.access: Free, a solitary tree on open agricultural/village land near Zabudišová; described as reachable, no gate mentioned.
trees.transport: Rural village lane, Bošáca; nearest town Nové Mesto nad Váhom roughly 15 minutes by car.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the solitary pear tree on open land, its flesh famously pink rather than white when cut. It stands near Zabudisova, 350m from the prize-winning apple tree.

trees.name: The Wild Pear of Lysica Hill

location.address: foot of Lysica Hill, Bošáca, Nové Mesto nad Váhom District

trees.access: Free, open hillside at the foot of Lysica Hill above the Bošácka valley; the tree is described as a landmark for local paragliders and model-aircraft flyers, which implies open recreational ground rather than fenced land. No gate, ticket or access restriction mentioned in any source; not confirmed via OSM tags (Overpass query failed from this environment).
trees.transport: Rural hillside above Bošáca village; nearest town Nové Mesto nad Váhom, roughly 15 minutes by car, same as the other two Bošáca trees. No public transport stop at the tree itself.
trees.story:
Nobody planted Bošáca's third champion tree. A bird did, or the wind: a seed from a cultivated pear somewhere nearby landed on the sunny slope of Lysica Hill and took root on its own. Roughly 150 years later it is a wild pear ten metres tall, with a trunk 195 centimetres round.

That sets it apart from its two famous neighbours in Zabudišová, four kilometres away. The pink pear and the heirloom apple there were planted for their fruit. This one is Pyrus pyraster, the wild species, and big self-seeded pears like it are part of what the White Carpathian landscape around the Bošácka valley looks like: a valley that grew fruit for generations, scattering its own trees across the hills.

On Lysica it has become a landmark for the paragliders and model-aircraft flyers who use the hill. In 2024 the municipality nominated it for Slovakia's Tree of the Year, and it won with 2,298 votes, the village's third national title after the pear in 2015 and the apple in 2017. At the European final in 2025 it placed fifth, with 23,729 votes.

The contest's own account and an independent Slovak news report both give its age as 150 years.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as a wild pear about 10 metres tall with a trunk 195 centimetres round. It stands on the open slope at the foot of Lysica Hill, 4 km from Bošáca's two other champion fruit trees in Zabudišová.
